title: Microstructure of Lignocellulosic Biopolymeric Membranes: Implications for Functional Applications
content: Lignocellulosic membranes were formed from materials obtained from plant fibers composed of cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin and were morphologically characterized. These materials have aroused increasing interest due to their potential applications in industry due to their sustainability and biodegradability. Research focused on how interactions between natural binders and fibrous materials (FM) affect the structural and functional properties of membranes. The advantages of using natural binders over synthetic ones were tested, as well as their impact on morphological properties such as strength, porosity and density of the membranes [1].
